passages.original: scholion ibid. p. 353 R. ὅρα δὲ πῶς ἐπιλογικῶς ἤρξατο ἀπὸ συνηγόρων ἐκβολῆς, ὥςπερ καὶ ὁ Δημοσθένης. cf. schol. or. I 69 ἀξιοῦσι τινὲς μέμφεσθαι τῷ ῥήτορι ἐν ἀγῶνι συνηγόρων ἐκβολὴν ποιησαμένῳ, δέον ἐν ἐπιλόγῳ.
passages.english: Scholion, ibid. p. 353 R.: "Notice how he began in the manner of an epilogue, with the dismissal of the advocates, just as Demosthenes also [did]." Cf. scholion on Oration I 69: "Some think it right to find fault with the orator for having made a dismissal of the advocates in the [main] contest [of the speech], when it ought [to come] in the epilogue."
passages.notes: "Scholion ibid. p. 353 R." and "cf. schol. or. I 69" are the editor's Latin citations of the sources, kept as references. "R." probably refers to the page numbering of Reiske's edition. "Dismissal of the advocates" (συνηγόρων ἐκβολή) is a rhetorical term for the move by which a speaker discredits or forestalls the opponent's supporting speakers. "Epilogue" (ἐπίλογος) means the peroration, the closing part of a speech. ἐν ἀγῶνι probably means the main argumentative part of the speech, as opposed to the epilogue; the bracketed words reflect that reading.
